question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress Gateway binds, and if so what explicit guardrail must be required?
rationale: The request would move protection for a powerful reachable Gateway surface from OpenClaw-managed auth to external network controls, and current code intentionally blocks that boundary.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
options.body: Preserve the current shared-secret or trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and document trusted-proxy/password as the supported private-network path.

options.title: Sponsor Private-Ingress Opt-In
options.body: Allow reachable no-auth only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Reject Core No-Auth Reachability
options.body: Close this direction as not planned and direct users to token/password, Tailscale Serve, or trusted-proxy deployments.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current shared-secret or trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and document trusted-proxy/password as the supported private-network path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-main and latest-release provenance for the startup guard being discussed.
